summary:
Observed facts. The #134 implementation is coherent and complete in the frozen tree: scripts/duo-build.cjs (check/start/review/resume; pinned goal+task+reference hashes; per-round frozen tree+manifest+diff+index+commits+request+invocation+prompt; read-only peer invocation; recursion guard; snapshot-drift rejection before, during and after review; initial review plus at most three repair rounds), skills/duo-build/SKILL.md, docs/duo-build.md, the bin/specflow.js `duo-build` entry (tree/bin/specflow.js:29-34) and 20 tests in tests/scripts/duo-build.test.js. AC-4 untracked/uncommitted capture is directly demonstrated on this round: manifest.json:1438/1502/1974 list scripts/duo-build.cjs, skills/duo-build/SKILL.md and the test file, none of which appear in diff.patch (which covers only .gitignore, README.md, bin/specflow.js, docs/should-i-use-specflow.md, install-hooks.sh, jest.config.js, setup-project.sh, skills/*, templates/*) and index.patch is empty. Direction matches the run goal and bounded objective (goal.md): the builder stays interactive, the peer is read-only, and status()/docs/duo-build.md:61-63 state acceptance never means merged or deployed (AC-6). The batch assumption "existing installers already copy all scripts and skill directories" is verified rather than assumed: install-hooks.sh:234-257 copies scripts/*.cjs and every skills/* directory into .claude/.codex/.agents, setup-project.sh:150-153/202-211 does the same and then delegates to install-hooks.sh (setup-project.sh:718), and tests/scripts/duo-build.test.js:120-123 exercises the install-hooks path for both runtimes.

Prior findings against resolution evidence. F1 (round-002) remains resolved: full-tests.txt shows `npm test -- --runInBand`, exit 0, 41/41 suites, 922/922 tests passed with no skipped/todo line, including PASS tests/scripts/duo-build.test.js; contract-tests.txt shows `npm test -- contracts --runInBand`, exit 0, 27/27 suites, 626/626 passed — satisfying CLAUDE.md Rule 3 and Rule 4 for a change adding scripts/*.cjs under PROJ-003 and a new CLI command. The 922 count is internally consistent with the 921 recorded in round-003 plus exactly one new test. F2/F3 are now resolved: evidence/duo-build/codex-auth.txt records real `codex --version` (codex-cli 0.154.0, exit 0) and `codex login status` (exit 0, combined output carrying "Logged in using ChatGPT" on stderr), which I independently checked against the gate at scripts/duo-build.cjs:51-53 — `/Logged in using\s+\S/i` matches that actual wording, and because the helper passes `combineOutput: true` the stderr-only signal is captured, which was the precise failure mode F3 hypothesised. Both current-helper readiness checks are recorded live with exit 0 and the post-fix record shape (`artifactAccess: "not yet verified"`, `enforcedMode`), so the Codex readiness gate is live-verified, not double-only; the peer version string cross-corroborates proof/codex/stderr.txt:1 (OpenAI Codex v0.154.0). The self-raised "readable-status" item is implemented at duo-build.cjs:204 (blocker leads with `id: action`) and covered by a passing test at tests/scripts/duo-build.test.js:134-140. Earlier round-001 symlink and round-003 exit-code observations are also addressed (files() drops node_modules at any depth, duo-build.cjs:59; cli() now returns 0/1/2 for both review and resume, duo-build.cjs:240).

Live versus simulated. Confirmed live this round: invocation.json is `claude -p` with `--tools Read,Glob,Grep`, `--allowedTools Read,Glob,Grep`, `dontAsk`, `--safe-mode`, no write tool, and my session had only Read/Glob/Grep — AC-4 "reviewer cannot edit product files" holds; check() ran before I was launched. Confirmed live earlier: proof/codex/stderr.txt is a genuine `codex exec` transcript (v0.154.0, sandbox read-only, approval never) where Codex read the frozen files, independently reran the fixture and returned the accept recorded in proof/codex/review.json; that record carries the pre-fix `permission` field and is correctly labelled pre-correction in live-cycle.md:50-52. Simulated and labelled as such: all provider responses in the unit suite (tests/scripts/duo-build.test.js:11-23), and the interactive Claude host in the reverse-direction smoke (runner setting), stated in batch.json:6 and live-cycle.md:27-33. A real correction/re-review cycle is durable across round-002 (F1/F2), round-003 (F3) and this round (AC-5/AC-7).

Status distinctions. Implemented and locally tested with full and contract suites green and three real peer reviews executed. Nothing is committed, merged, deployed, CI-run or customer-validated; no PR/CI export is claimed, so none is required. The jest.config.js change excluding /.specflow/duo/ is in-scope housekeeping that removes frozen snapshot copies from test discovery and excludes no product test path (41 suites still run). Acceptance here covers only the stated batch scope — Issue #134 AC-1 through AC-7 local implementation and verification — and is not a release approval; required CI, release and human gates remain outstanding, as does the ticket's DoD item that native interactive launch be exercised.

unrelated: tree/evidence/duo-build/unit-tests.txt is stale: it reports 13 tests while tests/scripts/duo-build.test.js now defines 20. live-cycle.md:7 repeats the 13 figure and line 52 annotates it as historical, and full-tests.txt supersedes it with zero skips, so this is not blocking — but the artifact should be refreshed or deleted so it cannot be read as the current suite size.

The customer-visible instruction `/duo-build #905` (README.md addition in diff.patch:21-27, tree/docs/duo-build.md:21, tree/skills/duo-build/SKILL.md:12) is still unverified as a native Claude Code slash invocation from within this snapshot; no .claude/commands/duo-build.md ships (manifest.json:2-9 lists only readme-audit and readme-restructure) and skills install to .claude/skills. The batch explicitly defers native interactive launch, so it is out of scope here, but it is a prominent published value worth confirming before release and before closing the ticket's DoD.

tree/skills/README.md still documents only specflow-loop-selector and does not mention the duo-build skill; tree/templates/AGENTS.md work routing likewise does not say which route duo-build belongs to.

The new .gitignore rule `.specflow/duo/` (diff.patch:9-11) means live-cycle.md's relative links to the round records resolve only on the author's machine. The two proof files were force-included as explicit evidence, but the ticket's DoD "Live build/review/correction/re-review artifacts are readable" will need a deliberate export of the round-002/003/004 records too.

check() hardcodes enforcedMode strings at tree/scripts/duo-build.cjs:54 rather than deriving them from invocation(). They match this round's invocation.json today, but a future flag change would leave the durable readiness record silently misstating the enforced mode.

Snapshot capture still aborts the whole run on any symlink outside node_modules (tree/scripts/duo-build.cjs:23-34). A repository with a legitimately committed symlink cannot be reviewed at all; recording symlinks as an explicit unsupported-entry list in snapshot-policy.json would degrade more gracefully.

Stale-lock recovery at tree/scripts/duo-build.cjs:134-138 rethrows any process.kill error whose code is not ESRCH, so a corrupt or non-numeric review.lock (NaN pid) leaves the run unreviewable until the file is deleted by hand.

validateReview only checks that requiredReads appear in the peer's self-reported inspected array (tree/scripts/duo-build.cjs:125-127); a peer can list paths it never opened. The derived label at line 190 honestly says "peer reported", but the underlying claim remains unverifiable from the helper's side.

batch.json:5 still summarises the review history as "real Claude review found F1/F2" without naming F3 from round-003; the resolutions block and live-cycle.md:45-52 do record F3 accurately, so nothing is misstated overall, but the claim line is one round out of date.
